headline: Board continues Avesta Housing Development Corporation tax appeal hearing to September 14, 2026
summary: The Board of Assessment Review approved its August 17, 2026 minutes and found it had jurisdiction over Avesta Housing Development Corporation's appeal of assessments on properties including 307 Cumberland Avenue and several Elm Street addresses. After hearing arguments from the taxpayer and the Assessor, the Board continued the hearing to September 14, 2026.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 17, 2026 meeting by a vote of 3-0.
Found that the Board had jurisdiction over the Avesta Housing Development Corporation appeal by a vote of 3-0.
Continued the Avesta Housing Development Corporation appeal hearing to 11 a.m. on September 14, 2026, by a vote of 3-0.

plain_text:
Board of Assessment Review 
Monday, August 24, 2026, 9:00 AM 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Eric Larsson, Chair 
Dale Knapp 
Lee Lowry 
 
The meeting convened at 9:00 a.m. on August 24, 2026 via Zoom. 
 
Attendees: Board members Eric Larsson, Chair, Dale Knapp, Lee Lowry, Attorney Jonathan 
Hunter representing the board, City Assessor Elisa Marr (joined at 9:17 a.m.), Assistant City 
Assessor Matthew Caton, Attorney Michael Goldman representing the city, Attorney Henry 
Barkley representing the taxpayer, Andrew Altmaier and Patrick Hess representing the taxpayer, 
and board assistant Annie James. 
Board attendance was taken by roll call. No members of the public were present at the start of 
the hearing. 
 
Approve the Minutes of the August 17, 2026 Board of Assessment Review Meeting 
 
Board Chair Larsson moved to approve the minutes of the August 17, 2026 Board of Assessment 
Review Meeting. Board member Knapp seconded the motion, which was approved by a roll call 
vote of (3-0). 
 
Appeal of Assessments re: 307 Cumberland Avenue, CBL 033 N018001; 220 Oxford 
Street, CBL 033 N003001; 67 Elm Street, CBL 033 N001001; 61 Elm Street, CBL 033 
N004001; and 55 Elm Street, CBL 033 N006001; Owner Avesta Housing Development 
Corporation 
 
Board Chair Larsson initiated discussion regarding Board jurisdiction over the appeal. Board 
members reviewed potential conflicts of interest, and none were identified. Attorney Goldman 
confirmed that the Assessor formally withdraws its objection to the Section 706-A issue. The 
following individuals spoke: Eric Larsson, Attorney Hunter, Attorney Barkley, Attorney 
Goldman, Dale Knapp, Lee Lowry. 
 
Elisa Marr joined the meeting at 9:17 a.m. 
 
Board Chair Larsson began reviewing the meeting agenda and the submitted materials. A clerical
error was identified in the Assessor’s response: the date April 23, 2026, was corrected to 
February 24, 2026. Attorney Hunter presented the dates as amended. With no objections from 
the parties or the Board, the timeline was accepted as modified. The following individuals spoke: 
Eric Larsson, Attorney Hunter, Attorney Barkley, Attorney Goldman. 
 
The Board continued discussing the jurisdictional aspects of the appeal. Board Chair Larsson 
moved to find the Board had jurisdiction and Board member Knapp seconded, which was 
approved by a roll call vote of (3-0). The following individuals spoke: Eric Larsson, Attorney 
Goldman, Attorney Barkley, Attorney Hunter. 
 
A break was called at 9:48 a.m. 
 
The meeting resumed at 10:01 a.m. 
 
Board Chair Larsson opened the hearing of Avesta Housing Development Corporation’s appeal. 
Attorney Barkley, representing the taxpayer, presented their argument. The following individuals 
spoke: Attorney Barkley, Andrew Altmaier, Patrick Hess. 
The following Exhibits were displayed on the screen: Applicant’s PowerPoint, Applicant’s 
Exhibits O, N, B, D, E, Q, Assessor’s Exhibits 15, 14 
 
A break was called at 10:59 a.m. 
 
The meeting resumed at 11:06 a.m. 
 
The Assessor and Board then asked the Applicant questions. The following individuals spoke: 
Attorney Goldman, Andrew Altmaier, Patrick Hess, Attorney Barkley, Eric Larsson, Dale 
Knapp, Lee Lowry, Matthew Caton, Attorney Hunter. 
The following Exhibits were displayed on the screen: Applicant’s Exhibit X, Applicant’s 
PowerPoint. 
 
Board Chair Larsson invited the Assessors to present their response. The following individuals 
spoke: Attorney Goldman, Elisa Marr, Matthew Caton. 
The following Exhibits were displayed on the screen: Applicant’s Exhibit H, Assessor’s 
Response, Assessor’s Exhibit 9. 
 
A break was called at 12:20 p.m. 
 
The meeting resumed at 12:27 p.m. 
 
The Applicant and Board then asked the Assessor questions. The following individuals spoke: 
Attorney Barkley, Matthew Caton, Eric Larsson, Dale Knapp, Attorney Hunter. 
The following Exhibits were displayed on the screen: Applicant’s Exhibits H, Assessor’s Exhibit 
14, 15, 9. 
 
A break was called at 1:00 p.m.
The meeting resumed at 1:33 p.m. 
 
The Assessor continued answering questions. The following individuals spoke: Attorney Hunter, 
Matthew Caton, Attorney Goldman, Eric Larsson, Dale Knapp, Attorney Barkley, Andrew 
Altmaier, Patrick Hess. 
The following Exhibits were displayed on the screen: Applicant’s Exhibits H, Z, Assessor’s 
Exhibit 9, the Assessor’s Response. 
 
Board Chair Larsson invited the appellant to close their argument. The following individuals 
spoke: Attorney Barkley. 
 
Board Chair Larsson invited the Assessors to close their argument. The following individuals 
spoke: Attorney Goldman, Matthew Caton. 
 
Board Chair Larsson invited the appellant to rebut. The following individuals spoke: Attorney 
Barkley. 
 
Attorney Hunter provided a summary of the Board’s role as the decision-making body. The 
following individuals spoke: Attorney Hunter, Eric Larsson, Lee Lowry, Dale Knapp. 
 
Board Chair Larsson opened the hearing to public comment. No members of the public were 
present.  
 
The Board closed the public portion of the meeting and motioned to continue the hearing at 11 
a.m. on September 14, 2026, which was moved by Board Chair Larsson and seconded by Board 
member Lowry, and passed by a roll call vote of (3-0). The following individuals spoke: Eric 
Larsson, Annie James, Attorney Barkley, Dale Knapp, Lee Lowry, Attorney Hunter, Attorney 
Goldman. 
 
Adjournment 
 
Board member Knapp moved and Board member Lowry seconded the motion to adjourn, which 
passed by a roll call vote of (3-0). The meeting concluded at 3:14 p.m.
